<!--
  Release notes for SherlockEQ 0.1.2.

  Authored as HTML so Sparkle's update dialog renders the formatting;
  GitHub renders inline HTML in release notes the same way.
-->

<h2>SherlockEQ 0.1.2</h2>

<p>
  Moves the system-audio permission into Apple's narrower "System Audio
  Recording" bucket on macOS 15+, makes audio-engine failures actually
  tell you what went wrong, and bumps the minimum window size so the
  Equalizer and Tinnitus Notch screens fit without scrolling.
</p>

<h3>Changed</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Permission moved to "System Audio Recording".</strong>
    Previously SherlockEQ asked for "Screen &amp; System Audio Recording"
    — the same broad permission used by screen-recording apps like Loom
    and Microsoft Teams. macOS 15 Sequoia introduced a narrower,
    audio-only TCC bucket called "System Audio Recording" — where
    Audio Hijack and Audio Routing Kit live — and SherlockEQ now uses
    that instead. On macOS 14, it appears under Screen Recording in
    Settings (Apple hadn't split the UI yet); on macOS 15+, it has its
    own row.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Minimum window size bumped (1400×740 → 1400×860).</strong>
    The Equalizer and Tinnitus Notch screens now fit without scrolling
    at the smallest allowed size.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Fixed</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>"Graph not attached" replaced with the real reason.</strong>
    When the audio engine failed to start, the banner used to say
    "Audio engine: Graph not attached" — a generic message that masked
    the actual problem (a format build failure, an unexpected
    sample-rate mismatch). The engine now surfaces the specific cause
    so the notice is actionable.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>If you installed 0.1.0 or 0.1.1</h3>

<p>
  On first launch after upgrading, macOS will prompt for the new
  "System Audio Recording" permission. Grant it, then quit and
  relaunch SherlockEQ — TCC permissions don't take effect for a
  running process until the next launch.
</p>

<p>
  Your previous grant under "Screen &amp; System Audio Recording" is
  orphaned but harmless. If you want to clean it up: System Settings
  → Privacy &amp; Security → Screen &amp; System Audio Recording →
  select SherlockEQ → click the minus button. Optional.
</p>

<h3>Not a medical device</h3>

<p>
  SherlockEQ is not a healthcare or medical application. It does not
  diagnose, treat, measure, or monitor any hearing condition, tinnitus,
  or disability. For concerns about your hearing, consult a doctor,
  audiologist, or licensed healthcare professional.
</p>
